role: client-specific marketing-grade research (Atlas) — feeds website, creatives, marketing
growth_policy: Add new cases from rejected/revised research reports, from weak-hook or weak-creative complaints, and from any niche/location where local data was thin.

cases.input: workflow_step_id=<uuid> for a dental clinic in Houston, TX (client data already in the Neon clients table).
cases.expected_behavior: Read the client from the Neon clients table (CRM-synced) — NOT Radar/S3. Websearch and analyze AT LEAST 10 real, named local competitors; for each capture service, USPs/positioning, reviews (rating + count + recurring praise AND complaints), and website notes; then synthesize the positioning gap and the proof bar; write each competitor to the Neon competitors table.
expected_response_traits: each with service + USPs + reviews (praise AND complaints)
unacceptable_patterns: uses or asks for Radar/S3 reports

cases.input: workflow_step_id=<uuid> for a boutique fitness studio in Miami, FL.
cases.expected_behavior: From the clients data + competitor analysis, find a differentiated positioning gap that none of the competitors own, and recommend a one-line positioning + primary CTA, grounded in evidence.
expected_response_traits: positioning gap tied to the real Miami market
evidence for the gap (from competitor reviews/market)
unacceptable_patterns: me-too positioning a competitor already owns

cases.input: workflow_step_id=<uuid>. Produce the hooks & angles for a dental clinic targeting new patients.
cases.expected_behavior: Produce AT LEAST 10 hooks across DISTINCT angles. Each hook must be specific/concrete (real number+outcome+timeframe), emotionally driven (tied to a real audience pain from reviews/research), mechanism-based where possible, differentiated (exploits the positioning gap), and proof-backed. Give per hook: line + angle + emotional driver + proof + why it beats competitors.
expected_response_traits: 10+ hooks across distinct angles (not 10 versions of one)
each specific with a real number/outcome/timeframe
each tied to a real emotional driver/pain
each paired with proof and a 'why it beats competitors'
unacceptable_patterns: 'best dentist in town' / 'your trusted partner' / vague hooks
hooks not tied to audience pain

cases.input: workflow_step_id=<uuid>. Give the website direction for the dental clinic.
cases.expected_behavior: Produce a buildable page direction: a specific color theme (with why it fits + how it differentiates from competitors), purposeful motion/animation, typography, and content with the chosen hook in the hero plus supporting angles, objection-handling built from real competitor complaints, a proof architecture, and ONE conversion goal — framed knowing the page will be marketed (mobile-first, message-match).
expected_response_traits: objection handling from real competitor complaints
unacceptable_patterns: 'use a modern design' / generic visual advice
hooks bolted on, not in the content

cases.input: workflow_step_id=<uuid>. Give the creatives (ad images/videos) direction for the dental clinic, matched to the website theme.
cases.expected_behavior: Specify premium, scroll-stopping ad creatives that match the website's color theme and are designed to drive purchases: real/premium visuals (no stock), short video (<15s) with the hook in the first ~3s, and a STRONG on-image/on-video text style (first overlay carries the hook, large/bold/high-contrast/centred, ~5-7 words, brand fonts+theme colors). For each creative give the concept, format, the exact overlay hook line, the angle it serves, and why this audience will BUY.
expected_response_traits: short video with hook in first ~3s
each creative: concept + format + overlay hook line + angle + why it sells
ties back to the brief's hooks + the website theme
unacceptable_patterns: decorative creative with no text hook
off-theme colors (ad doesn't match the site)

cases.input: A direct request whose whole message is a malformed / non-UUID client id.
cases.expected_behavior: Detect the invalid client_id, do NOT fabricate data, ask for a valid UUID or mark intake blocked.

cases.input: workflow_step_id=<uuid>. Niche+location with very little local online presence.
cases.expected_behavior: Note the local-data gap, expand to metro/state/USA-wide, and clearly label what is local vs inferred — still delivering 10+ competitors and strong hooks.

cases.input: workflow_step_id=<uuid>. Produce 5 synchronized landing-page variations with 15+ sections each.
cases.expected_behavior: Deliver 5 variations sharing one core message but meaningfully different angles, each with 15+ coherent sections (no clashing colors/tones across sections), each carrying a distinct hook.
expected_response_traits: each variation carries a distinct strong hook

cases.input: Any research job with a workflow_step_id.
cases.expected_behavior: Save the brief to the workspace, write research_reports + the >=10 competitor rows + the pending research_approval to Neon per the Worker Contract, store the self-check in agent_runs.self_check_score, and return the file path + handoff summary. Do NOT contact Slack.
expected_response_traits: research_reports + competitors (>=10) + approval written to Neon
unacceptable_patterns: returns only chat text, nothing saved

cases.expected_behavior: Frame the ENTIRE brief for marketing/conversion: the research exists to market the client's service and make more people buy. Every section (competitors, hooks, website, creatives) should serve get-found / get-chosen / get-bought, and use ONLY the clients data + websearch (no Radar/S3).
expected_response_traits: hooks + website + creatives all aligned to selling the service
unacceptable_patterns: academic/neutral research with no marketing intent
